edges.description: PHOX2B governs autonomic neuronal development, and the tumours that arise are of that lineage. The intervening steps are not established in the sources cited here.
Carriers frequently have Hirschsprung disease alongside the tumours. The intervening steps are not established in the sources cited.
The authors link PHOX2B to normal respiratory patterning; the mechanism is not established in the sources cited.
The disturbed lineage gives rise to tumours across the neuroblastic spectrum.
Disturbed differentiation is expressed in the tumour phenotype as a skew towards ganglion cell maturation in the 2015 series; the mechanism is not established.
The same skew in the 2015 series includes ganglioneuroblastomas, with both neuroblastic and ganglion cell components.

The undifferentiated end of the spectrum is also produced, and the two non-polyalanine series disagree on how often: mostly invasive neuroblastoma in the 2005 CCHS series, mostly differentiated tumours in the 2015 series. The mechanism is not established.

nodes.description: Sleep-associated hypoventilation from impaired central ventilatory control, the defining feature of congenital central hypoventilation syndrome and of late-onset forms. It is mainly a feature of polyalanine expansion carriers, but also occurs in carriers of the non-polyalanine variants. Curated as a phenotype here and as a disease in Congenital_Central_Hypoventilation_Syndrome.

nodes.description: The tumours arising in PHOX2B carriers are of the sympathetic nervous system lineage. In the 2015 series of non-polyalanine repeat mutation carriers they were predominantly differentiated, ganglioneuroma and ganglioneuroblastoma more often than neuroblastoma, although the 2005 CCHS series found invasive neuroblastoma in 6 of 13 such carriers. The skew towards maturation in the later series is the clearest clue that what the variant disturbs is the differentiation programme of autonomic neuroblasts rather than proliferation alone. The entry does not claim more than that, because no cited source establishes the mechanism.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline variant in PHOX2B, the paired-like homeobox gene that is the master regulator of autonomic nervous system development. Two variant classes behave differently: polyalanine repeat expansions, and non-polyalanine repeat missense, frameshift or truncating variants. The difference in tumour risk between them is roughly thirty-fold, which is the central fact of this predisposition.

evidence.reference_title: Germline mutations of the paired-like homeobox 2B (PHOX2B) gene in neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: PHOX2B, therefore, stands as the first gene for which germline mutations predispose to NB.

nodes.description: Congenital absence of enteric ganglia, a neurocristopathy that frequently accompanies the tumour predisposition. It is curated as its own disease; it is recorded here as a phenotype because it is part of how carriers present. Six of thirteen carriers in the tumour series had congenital central hypoventilation syndrome and/or Hirschsprung disease, and the original germline report included a patient with the Hirschsprung disease and neuroblastoma association.

evidence.snippet: Germline non-polyalanine repeat expansion mutations in PHOX2B (PHOX2B NPARM) predispose to peripheral neuroblastic tumors (PNT), frequently in association with other neurocristopathies: Hirschsprung disease (HSCR) or congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS).

nodes.description: Neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma. The risk depends strongly on variant class: about 45 per cent for non-polyalanine repeat mutations against about 1 to 2 per cent for polyalanine expansions. In the original series the counts were 6 of 13 patients with a missense or frameshift variant against 2 of 161 with an in-frame expansion. Against a general-population neuroblastoma incidence of about 1 in 10,000, even the low-risk class is raised.

nodes.description: Neuroblastoma proper, the least differentiated end of the neuroblastic spectrum. The two series of non-polyalanine repeat mutation carriers disagree: in the 2005 CCHS series neuroblastoma was the usual tumour (6 of 13 carriers of a missense or frameshift variant), whereas in the 2015 series of thirteen tumour patients only one tumour was a differentiating neuroblastoma, though four others were poorly differentiated. The original report found neuroblastoma in a familial case and in a patient with Hirschsprung disease.
